28. As regard, this contention of learned AR of respondents that petitioners were not the employees of the 
BBMB but were the employees of BCB, the same is devoid of merit as Discharge certificate was issued by the 
BBMB. Moreover, as per respondents Beas Control Board was constituted in the year 1960. BCB was constituted in 
the year 1966 and all the projects were transferred from Beas Control Board to BCB in the year 1966 thereafter as per 
Section 79 of the Punjab Re-organization Act, BMB was constituted for administrative, maintenance and operation of 
various works as mentioned in Section 79 itself. Section 80(6) of the Punjab Re-organization Act provides that BMB 
constituted under Section 79 of the Act shall be re-named as BBMB when any of the components of the Beas Project 
has been transferred under sub-section 5 and the BCB shall cease to exist when all the component of the Beas Project 
have been so transferred. All the projects under BCB were completed in the year 1984 and BCB ceased to exist in 
1984. When all work of BCB stands transferred to BBMB so it cannot be said that BBMB is separate identity than 
BCB. Rather BCB has merged in BBMB. Moreover, Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jaswant Singh case (supra) in 
respect of work charged employees has no where stated that relief can be sought by work charged employees only 
against the BCB. So contention of Ld. AR of the respondents that BCB and BBMB are two separate entities is devoid 
of merit. 


29. So far this argument of AR for the respondents that the case is hopelessly time barred is concerned, the same 
is again devoid of merits as there was non-compliance of Rule 77 and 78 of Industrial Rules which has been 
reproduced above. Moreover, there is no limitation period prescribed for filing a reference. Moreover, reference was 
received in the year 2018. So far as case laws on the point of limitation the same are not attracted in the present case 
as there was no compliance of Judgment of Jaswant Singh case (Supra). Moreover, limitation was added in Section 
2A of the Act in the year 2010 (15.09.2010) and deceased workman was dismissed from service on 16.09.1977 and 
AR for respondents has failed to bring this fact that the aforesaid provision was retrospective. 


30. It is added here that in the present case, the reference was made under clause (d) of sub-section (1) of Section 
10 of the Act. It is not case filed under Section 2-A of the Act. Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as 


Raghubir Singh V/s General Manager, Haryana Roadways, Hissar (supra) has held as follow: 


“42. It is an undisputed fact that the dispute was raised by the workman after he was acquitted in the criminal 
case which was initiated at the instance of the respondent. Raising the industrial dispute belatedly and getting 
the same referred from the State Government to the Labour Court is for justifiable reason and the same is 
supported by law laid down by this Court in Calcutta Dock Labour Board (supra). Even assuming for the sake 
of the argument that there was a certain delay and latches on the part of the workman in raising the industrial 
dispute and getting the same referenced for adjudication, the Labour Court is statutorily duty bound to answer 
the points of dispute referred to it by adjudicating the same on merits of the case and it ought to have moulded 
the relief appropriately in favour of the workman. That has not been done at all by the Labour Court. Both the 
learned single Judge as well as the Division Bench of the High Court in its Civil Writ Petition and the Letters 
Patent Appeal have failed to consider this important aspect of the matter.” 


Even Hon'ble Supreme Court in para no.31 of the said judgment has held as follow: 


“31. The rejection of the reference by the Labour Court by answering the additional issue no. 2 regarding the 
delay latches and limitation without adjudicating the points of dispute referred to it on the merits amounts to 
failure to exercise its statutory power under Section I1A of the Act. Therefore, we have to interfere with the 
impugned award of the Labour Court and the judgment & order of the High Court as it has erroneously 
confirmed the award of the Labour Court without examining the relevant provisions of the Act and decisions of 
this Court referred to supra on the relevant issue regarding the limitation.” 


31. Hon'ble Supreme Court has also referred in the said case decision of Ajaib Singh v. The Sirhind_Co- 
Operative Marketing Cum- Processing Service Society Limited & Anr.(AIR 1999 Supreme Court 1351), wherein, 


Court has opined that relief cannot be denied to the workman merely on the ground of delay, stating that:- 


“10. It follows, therefore, that the provisions of Article 137 of the Schedule to Limitation Act, 1963 are not 
applicable to the proceedings under the act and that the relief under it cannot be denied to the workman merely 
on the ground of delay. The plea of delay if raised by the employer is required to be proved as a matter of fact 
by showing the real prejudice and not as a merely hypothetical defence. No reference to the labour court can be 
generally questioned on the ground of delay alone. Even in a case where the delay in shown to be existing, the 
tribunal, labour court or board, dealing with the case can appropriately mould the relief by declining to grant

back wages to the workman till the date he raised the demand regarding his illegal retrenchment/ termination

following scheme of compensation is deemed fit by this Tribunal: 


iv. Workcharged employee who has completed 5 years of service or more shall be entitled for Rs.50,000/- along

wife was Smt. Shanti Bai and Kaliram is his son from his first wife. His another wife is Smt. Sushila Bai and Rajesh 
is son of the Deceased Employee Kallu from his second wife Sushila Bai. Both Kaliram and Rajesh, who are sons of 
the Deceased Employee Kallu from his two wives, have placed their claim for compassionate appointment as a 
dependant son of their deceased father Kallu. But both cannot be granted compassionate appointment. Hence, till the 
dispute is resolved, the process has been put on hold. 


The Rajesh appeared in this case also as an intervener. The matter was sent by this Tribunal to Mediation 
Centre of Hon’ble High Court of M.P. as it involved dispute between the sons of the deceased employee and there 
were chances for conciliation, but Mediation failed. 


Affidavits and documents have been filed from all the sides, to be referred to as and when require. 


I have heard argument of Learned Counsel for the Applicant Kaliram Mr. Mukesh Mishra and Mr. Neeraj 
Kewat Learned Counsel for Management. The intervener Rajesh did not appear. I have gone through the records as 
well. 


From records, it is established that the two claimants Kaliram, the Applicant and the Rajesh are sons of the 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : फरवरी 7, 2026/माध 18, 1947 659 


deceased employee Kallu from his two wives. Kaliram is his son from first wife whereas Rajesh is his son from his 
second wife. 


Undisputedly, the Deceased Employee was Hindu, hence Hindu Marriage Act, 1956 shall apply in his case. 


It is established that even if the Marriage of the deceased employee Kallu with his second wife when his 
marriage with his first wife was not dissolved be considered void, the son from his second marriage will be entitled to 
inheritance with the son from his first wife. 


It would have been better that the parties would have settled this dispute within the family. One side of 
dependants would have agreed for post death benefits and other side for compassionate appointment. That would have 
been the best solution which could not be reached on in this case. 


Since, Applicant Kaliram has been sponsored by the legally wedded wife of the deceased employee as his 
dependant son for the purpose of compassionate appointment; he has a superior claim as compared to the intervener, 
Rajesh, who is son of the deceased employee from his second wife. Hence, on the basis of this discussion and 
findings, the reference is answered as follows. 


AWARD 


The applicant Kaliram is held entitled to be considered by the Management of WCL for compassionate 
appointment being son of deceased employee Kallu. If, his claim is found otherwise not fit to be entertained, the 
Management may consider claim of Rajesh for his appointment on compassionate ground being dependant son of 
deceased Kallu. 


The reference stands answered accordingly. 
No order as to cost.

As per letter dated 11/12/2020 by the Government of India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi, the reference is 
made to this Tribunal under Section-10 of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (in short the ‘Act’)as per Notification 
No. L-22012/45/2020-(IR(CM-ID)) dt. 11/12/2020. The dispute under reference relates to: 


“Whether the demand of the Samyukta Shramik Sangathit Asangathit Sangh, Korba for correction of the 
date of birth from 25.09.1960 to 10.05.1965 of the Workman Shri Santosh Kumar S/o Late Bhikham Ram, 
Sr. Data Entry Operator of Korba Area, SECL is legal and justified? If yes, to what relief the Samyukta 
Shramik Sangathit Asangathit Sangh, Korba is entitled?” 


After registering case on the basis of the reference, notices were issued to the parties. They appeared and 
filed their respective statement of claim and defense. 


Case of the Workman is mainly that, he was first appointed on 10.10.1983 with SECL Colliery in Sub-Area 
Chirmiri and was posted as Casual Mazdoor. He worked there till 05.09.1990, thereafter he joined as Data Entry 
Operator in the Korba Area. He was issued a last pay certificate from SECL Colliery showing his date of birth 
25.09.1960 whereas his date of birth is 10.05.1965, which he had disclosed at the time of his joining on 10.10.1983 
and had produced documents in this respect which are his Middle School Certificate cleared by him in 1976. He 
moved an application in the year 1991 and thereafter filed other applications dated 15.07.1993 and 28.05.1999 
requesting the Management at Korba to correct his date of birth, but no action was taken. Thereafter, he made a 
request to conduct an enquiry with respect to his date of birth and correct it by way of filing applications dated 
18.08.2002 and 25.07.200. The Office of the General management vide his letter dated 12.11.2002 and 11.03.2003 
sought same clarifications with respect to his contents which he submitted vide his letter dated 20.03.2003. No action 
was taken by Management and no enquiry was conducted. It is further his case that at the time of his first appointment 
on 10.10.1983 he submitted his domicile certificate, Class 87 School Certificate, Caste Certificate, preliminary 
description and employment card, issued from employment exchange, showing his date of birth 10.05.1965. In his 
service record also at SECL Colliery, his date of birth 10.05.1965 was recorded, but the Management unilaterally and 
arbitrarily changed his date of birth from 10.05.1965 to 25.09.1960 without intimating and without conducting an 
enquiry under his knowledge. The workman has also stated that, he was never informed about the Age Determining 
Committee in 1988 as claimed by Management. He was unjustly superannuated by Management on the basis of his 
wrong date of birth dated 10.09.1960 after attaining 60 years of age which is unjust, arbitrary and illegal. He has thus 
requested that setting-aside the order of his superannuation by Management on the basis of his date of birth 
10.09.1960, he be deemed to be reinstated with back-wages and as well consequential pre and post retiral benefits 
deeming him to be in continuous employment till date of his superannuation based on his correct date of birth 
1.6. 10.05.1965. 


Case of the Management is mainly that, the qualification for the Causal Mazdoor is illiterate. The workman 
did not produce any document with respect to his date of birth at the time of his first appointment, his date of birth 
10.09.1960 was recorded on the basis of information furnished by him in this respect. He accepted it and made his 
signatures in his service record. Thereafter, he was posted as Data Entry Operator in Korba. His last pay certificate 
was issued from the place of his earlier posting mentioning his date of birth as 10.06.1960 on the basis of his 
service record. 


It is further the case of the Management that in 1988, an Age Determination Committee was constituted to 
address disputes with respect to dates of birth of the Workmen, including the Applicant Workman, and the Committee 
submitted its report. The date of the birth of the Applicant Workman was found correct which was mentioned in his 
service records as 10.09.1960. The workman has wrongly been perusing and agitating against this decision of the 
Management to which he is not entitled to. It is further the case of the Management that, superannuation of the 
Workman after attaining 60 years on the basis of his date of birth recorded as 10.09.1960 is correct and just in law. 


Both the sides filed their affidavits as their examination-in-chief and which they have been cross-examined 
by their opposite party. Documentary evidence has also been filed and proved in form of RTI documents and other 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : फरवरी 7, 2026/माध 18, 1947 661 


photocopy documents to be referred to as and when require. 


I have heard argument of Mr. Tapan Kumar Chakravarti representative of the Union for the Workman and 
Mr. Neeraj Kewat for the Management. I have gone through the record as well. 


It comes out that case of Management is that, the Age Determining Committee was constituted in 1988 with 
respect to settling the dispute regarding the date of birth of certain workers including the Applicant Workman which 
files its report and found his date of birth as 10.09.1960 recorded in his service records as correct. 


Case of the Workman is that this Committee never informed the Workman to produce his side of evidences. 
He was never heard by this Committee, he was never informed of the findings of this Committee. He kept agitating 
against the entry with respect to his date of birth consistently even after 1988. In these circumstances, this Tribunal 
directed the Management to file the proceedings of the Age Determining Committee constituted in 1988 and its 
report. An affidavit was filed by Management that proceedings and report of the Age Determining Committee were 
not available, only an order dated 05.10.1988 passed by the Additional Chief Mining Engineer of SECL Colliery was 
filed in photocopy. 


Under National Coal Wage Agreement, Implementation Instructions 76 procedure for settlement of date of 
disputes with respect to date of birth of employees has been mention. The relevant portion is being reproduced as 
under 


Determination of the age at the time of appointment 
i) Matriculates. 


In the case of appointees who have passed Matriculation or equivalent examinations, the 
date of birth recorded in the said certificate shall be treated as correct date of birth and the same 
will not be altered under any circumstances. 


ii) Non-matriculates but educated. 


In the case of appointees who have pursued studies in a recognised educational institution, the 
date of birth recorded in the School Leaving Certificate, shall be treated as correct date of birth and, 
thesame will not be altered under any circumstances 


Undisputedly, in this case, the Workman had cleared its Class 87 examination (in 1976) ie; much 
before his appointment with the Management in 1983. His date of birth 1.6. 10.05.1965 is mentioned in the certificate. 
The Age Determining Committee is bound to rely on this Certificate till it is proved to be a non genuine. Since, the 
report of Age Determining Committee has not been produced by Management, hence, basis of the finding of the Age 
Determining Committee cannot be ascertained. It is not clear whether Age Determining Committee considered his 
educational certificate of the Workman as mentioned or not. This is also not established that, the Workman was 
informed about proceedings of the Age Determining Committee and was allowed to participate in the proceedings. 
Case of the Workman is that, neither he was informed nor did he participate in the proceedings, is supported by an 
Affidavit and cannot be disbelieved in the light of the circumstances as mentioned above. There is no affidavit of any 
Member of the Age Determining Committee to indicate that the Committee has noticed the Workman and allowed the 
Workman to participate in the proceedings. 


Since, the settled principle as mentioned in the Implementation Instructions 76, is that if the Workman is 
literate, his high school certificate and his middle school certificate in case he has not cleared his high school 
examination, will be relied upon for the date of his birth. Hence, on this basis, non acceptance of the date of birth of 
the Workman Santosh Kumar as 10.05.1965 as mentioned in his Middle School Certificate by the Management is 
held unjust, illegal and contrary to law. Consequently, the action of Management in superannuating the Workman 
after attaining 60 years on the basis of his date of birth 10.09.1960 is also held vitiated in law. 


In the light of above recorded findings the reference is answered as follows. 
AWARD 


Holding the demand of the Samyukta Shramik Sangathit Asangathit Sangh, Korba for correction of the 
date of birth from 25.09.1960 to 10.05.1965 of the Workman Shri Santosh Kumar S/o Late Bhikham Ram, Sr. 
Data Entry Operator of Korba Area, SECL as legal and justified, he is directed to be reinstated with all back-wages 
with all consequential pre as well post retrial benefits till the date of his superannuation based on his date of birth 
i.e. 10.05.1965 deeming him to be in continuous service of SECL. 


No order as to cost.

After registering the case on the basis of reference, notices were issued to the parties. They appeared and

The case of the workman is mainly that Deepak Modi was employed as General Mazdoor Category-I in the 
year 1980, work of loader was taken from him. He was not paid the wages admissible to loader inspite of the fact that 
job of loader was taken from him by the management, eventually, he died during service. Management and Union 
entered into the settlement with respect to claims of Deepak Modi on 13.03.2015, in which they agreed to recognize

the claim of Deepak Modi in this respect but did not pay. After his death, his son was appointed on compassionate 
grounds, he raised a dispute through Union after failure of conciliation and reference was made to this Tribunal. 
According to the workman refusal of pay of loader to the deceased Deepak Modi for the period which he had worked 
as loader though he was appointed as General Mazdoor Category-I is unjust, illegal and arbitrary. The Union has 
requested that his claim in this respect which is computed @ Rs. 1,70,000/- (One Lac Seventy Thousand Only) be 
granted along with interest @ 18% per annum. 


The case of the management is mainly that, Deepak Modi was initially appointed on 26.11.1979 as a 
General Mazdoor Category-I, he was regularized on 14.10.1981 and was transferred to Sarni Mines on 05.05.2011. 
He was never deployed as Pump Khalasi or Pump Operator or Loader by management at any point of time, hence he 
is not entitled to his claims. It is further the case of management that after Deepak Modi died in service, his son has 
been granted compassionate appointment and pension is being paid to his wife. It is also the case of management that 
there was no settlement with respect to the claims as made by the Union in the settlement dated 13.03.2015. 


During course of proceedings the son of deceased workman Deepak Modi who had raised dispute through 
Union also died and now union is prosecuting the reference. 


In Evidence, Union filed affidavit of wife and mother of deceased son of Deepak Modi as their examination- 
in-chief, they were cross-examined by Management. Workman side has filed and proved documents Ex-W/1 to Ex- 
W/3, to be referred to as and when require. 


Management has filed Office Order dated 20.10.2020 upgrading Deepak Modi to higher category. Copy of 
NCWA-II 29 photocopy settlement dated 13.03.2015, death certificate of Deepak Modi, letter to Regional Manager 
(Personnel) sent to the Union with respect to demand of Union for claim of Deepak Modi as stated above and other 
documents, to be referred to as and when required. Management has also filed affidavit of its witnesses as his 
examination-in-chief, he has been cross-examined by Union. 


I have heard argument of Learned Counsel Mr. Swapnil Khare for the Workman and Mr. Neeraj Kewat,

The reference itself is the issue for determination in the case in hand. 
The terms of the settlement dated 13.03.2015 are being reproduced as under:- 


1. The management agreed to allow Shri Deepak Modi Token No. 5148 to join in Sarni Mines of 
Pathakhera Area of WCL on the same post/grade in which he was working.

3. Management agreed that the period of absence from duty of Shri Deepak Modi will not be treated as 
break in service and will be counted for all other benefits. 


It is also agreed between the parties that other demands of the Union related to prior service of 
Shri Deepak Modi will be discussed among themselves and the outcome will be informed to this office

This resolves the dispute. Both the parties will inform the implementation position. 


It is clear from perusal of the settlement that in the settlement, parties agreed that other demands related to 
prior service of Deepak Modi will be discussed and outcome shall be informed within 90 days. 


It comes out from perusal of the record that Union sent representations with respect to claim of Deepak 
Modi regarding pay of loader as stated above, there is on record, reply of management filed and proved in which they 
have asked the Union to produce evidence in support of their this claim for the workman Deepak Modi though a

respect was filed by Union before management or this Tribunal. Hence, the claim that Deepak Modi worked as a

In light of above discussion and findings, the reference is answered as follows.-

As per letter dated 25/01/2022 by the Government of India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi, the reference 
has been made to this Tribunal under Section-10 of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (in short the ‘Act’)as per 
Notification No. 24(02)/2022-IR dt. 25/01/2022. The dispute under reference relates to: 


“Whether the action of the Management of Additional Director, Central Govt. Health Scheme (CGHS), 
Nagpur through its Contractor M/s Sidhivinayak Bahuddeshiya Seva Sahkari Sansthan Maryadit, Nagpur 
(MH) by terminating the services of Shri Mayur Bhandekar S/o Mr. Bhimrao Somaji Bandekar, DEO

the workman is entitled to?" 


After registering the case on the basis of reference, notices were issued to the parties. They appeared and filed their 
respective statement of claim in defense. 


The case of the workman, as taken by him in his statement of claim, is mainly that he was a Data Entry Operator, 
working with the establishment of Central Govt. Health Scheme (CGHS) in their CGHS Dispensary (Wellness 
Centre-[) at Raipur (CG) which is under supervision and control of Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 
Government of India. He worked there for more than three years continuously and regularly i.e. from 02.12.2017 to 
15.02.2021, when his services were terminated without following due process of law without any notice or 
compensation. He raised a dispute with the concerned Labour Commissioner (Central), which was referred to this 
Tribunal for adjudication after failure of conciliation, his work as Data Entry Operator was maintenance of frequent 
short term day to day issues arising in the hardware and software, uploading the application data and photographs for 
making plastic cards, online registration of patients, uploading online data reports and other works as specified by him 
in para 4 of his statement of claim. His work was supervised by the Officers and Employees of C.GH.LS., his transfer, 
joining from one office to other office and all other controls were directly done by the C.GH.S. without any 
intervention of anybody, his attendance was also made in biometric system maintained by C.GH.S. for their other 
regular and permanent employees. It is further the case of the workman that the outsourcing agency through which he

Reference may be taken of judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Jaggo v/s Union of India reported in 
(2024) SCC Online SC 3826, the relevant paragraphs of this judgment are being reproduced as follows:- 


“22. The pervasive misuse of temporary employment contracts, as exemplified in this case, reflects a broader 
systemic issue that adversely affects workers' rights and job security. In the private sector, the rise of the gig 
economy has led to an increase in precarious employment arrangements, often characterized by lack of 
benefits, job security, and fair treatment. Such practices have been criticized for exploiting workers and 
undermining labour standards. Government institutions, entrusted with upholding the principles of fairness 
and justice, bear an even greater responsibility to avoid such exploitative employment practices. When public 
sector entities engage in misuse of temporary contracts, it not only mirrors the detrimental trends observed in 
the gig economy but also sets a concerning precedent that can erode public trust in governmental operations. 


25. It is a disconcerting reality that temporary employees, particularly in government institutions, often face 
multifaceted forms of exploitation. While the foundational purpose of temporary contracts may have been to 
address short-term or seasonal needs, they have increasingly become a mechanism to evade long-term 
obligations owed to employees. These practices manifest in several ways: 


¢ Misuse of “Temporary” Labels:- Employees engaged for work that is essential, recurring, and integral to 
the functioning of an institution are often labelled as “temporary” or “contractual,” even when their roles 
mirror those of regular employees. Such misclassification deprives workers of the dignity, security, and 
benefits that regular employees are entitled to, despite performing identical tasks. 


¢ Arbitrary Termination:- Temporary employees are frequently dismissed without cause or notice, as seen in 
the present case. This practice undermines the principles of natural justice and subjects workers to a state of 
constant insecurity, regardless of the quality or duration of their service. 


¢ Lack of Career Progression:- Temporary employees often find themselves excluded from opportunities for 
skill development, promotions, or incremental pay raises. They remain stagnant in their roles, creating a 
systemic disparity between them and their regular counterparts, despite their contributions being equally 
significant. 


¢ Using Outsourcing as a Shield:- Institutions increasingly resort to outsourcing roles performed by 
temporary employees, effectively replacing one set of exploited workers with another. This practice not only 
perpetuates exploitation but also demonstrates a deliberate effort to bypass the obligation to offer regular 
employment. 


¢ Denial of Basic Rights and Benefits:- Temporary employees are often denied fundamental benefits such as 
pension, provident fund, health insurance, and paid leave, even when their tenure spans decades. This lack 
of social security subjects them and their families to undue hardship, especially in cases of illness, 
retirement, or unforeseen circumstances.” 


The principle laid down in the case of Jaggo (Supra) has been followed by Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case

of Shripal Vs. Nagar Nigam Ghaziabad in Civil Appeal No. 8157/2024 (2025 INSC 144). The relevant portion 


of the said judgment is being reproduced as follows:- 


“12. The evidence, including documentary material and undisputed facts, reveals that the Appellant 
Workmen performed duties integral to the Respondent Employer’s municipal functions specifically the 
upkeep of parks, horticultural tasks, and city beautification efforts. Such work is evidently perennial rather 
than sporadic or project-based. Reliance on a general “ban on fresh recruitment” cannot be used to deny 
labor protections to long serving workmen. On the contrary, the acknowledged shortage of Gardeners in the 
Ghaziabad Nagar Nigam reinforces the notion that these positions are essential and ongoing, not 
intermittent. By requiring the same tasks (planting, pruning, general upkeep) from the Appellant Workmen 
as from regular Gardeners but still compensating them inadequately and inconsistently the Respondent 
Employer has effectively engaged in an unfair labour practice. The principle of “equal pay for equal work,” 
repeatedly emphasized by this Court, cannot be casually disregarded when workers have served for extended 
periods in roles resembling those of permanent employees. Long-standing assignments under the Employer’s 
direct supervision belie any notion that these were mere short-term casual engagements. 


14. The Respondent Employer places reliance on Umadevi (supra) to contend that daily-wage or temporary 
employees cannot claim permanent absorption in the absence of statutory rules providing such absorption. 
However, as frequently reiterated, Uma Devi itself distinguishes between appointments that are “illegal” and 
those that are “irregular,” the latter being eligible for regularization if they meet certain conditions. More 
importantly, Uma Devi cannot serve as a shield to justify exploitative engagements persisting for years 
without the Employer undertaking legitimate recruitment. Given the record which shows no true contractor 
based arrangement and a consistent need for permanent horticultural staff the alleged asserted ban on fresh 
recruitment, though real, cannot justify indefinite daily-wage status or continued unfair practices. 


15. It is manifest that the Appellant Workmen continuously rendered their services over several years, 
sometimes spanning more than a decade. Even if certain muster rolls were not produced in full, the 
Employer’s failure to furnish such records—despite directions to do so—allows an adverse inference under 
well-established labour jurisprudence. Indian labour law strongly disfavors perpetual daily-wage or 
contractual engagements in circumstances where the work is permanent in nature. Morally and legally, 
workers who fulfil ongoing municipal requirements year after year cannot be dismissed summarily as 
dispensable, particularly in the absence of a genuine contractor agreement. At this juncture, it would be 
appropriate to recall the broader critique of indefinite “temporary” employment practices as done by a 


recent judgement of this court in Jaggo v. Union of India 


16. The High Court did acknowledge the Employer’s inability to justify these abrupt terminations. 
Consequently, it ordered re-engagement on daily wages with some measure of parity in minimum pay. 
Regrettably, this only perpetuated precariousness: the Appellant Workmen were left in a marginally 
improved yet still uncertain status. While the High Court recognized the importance of their work and hinted 
at eventual regularization, it failed to afford them continuity of service or meaningful back wages 
commensurate with the degree of statutory violation evident on record. 


17. In light of these considerations, the Employer’s discontinuation of the Appellant Workmen stands in 
violation of the most basic labour law principles. Once it is established that their services were terminated 
without adhering to Sections 6E and 6N of the U.P. Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, and that they were 
engaged in essential, perennial duties, these workers cannot be relegated to perpetual uncertainty. While 
concerns of municipal budget and compliance with recruitment rules merit consideration, such concerns do 
not absolve the Employer of statutory obligations or negate equitable entitlements. Indeed, bureaucratic 
limitations cannot trump the legitimate rights of workmen who have served continuously in de facto regular 
roles for an extended period. 18. The impugned order of the High Court, to the extent they confine the 
Appellant Workmen to future daily-wage engagement without continuity or meaningful back wages, is 
hereby set aside with the following directions:- 


I. The discontinuation of the Appellant Workmen’s services, effected without compliance with Section 6E 
and Section 6N of the U.P. Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, is declared illegal. All orders or communications 
terminating their services are quashed. In consequence, the Appellant Workmen shall be treated as 
continuing in service from thereof their termination, for all purposes, including seniority and continuity in 
service. 


II. The Respondent Employer shall reinstate the Appellant Workmen in their respective posts (or posts akin 
to the duties they previously performed) within four weeks from the date of this judgment. Their entire period 
of absence (from the date of termination until actual reinstatement) shall be counted for continuity of service 
and all consequential benefits, such as seniority and eligibility for promotions, if any. 


III. Considering the length of service, the Appellant Workmen shall be entitled to 50% of the back wages 
from the date of their discontinuation until their actual reinstatement. The Respondent Employer shall clear

disabled permanently or who died while in service. The provision will be implemented as follows.

monetary compensation would be governed by Clause 9.5.0.

suitable for employment and aged not more than 35 years provided that the age limit in case of employment of female 
spouse would be 45 years as given in Clause 9.5.0. In so far as male spouse is concerned, there would be no age limit 
regarding provision for employment.

unfitness under Clause 9.4.0, if no employment has been offered and the male dependant of the concerned worker is 
12 years and above in age, he will be kept on a live roster and would be provided employment commensurate with his 


678 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : FEBRUARY 7, 2026/MAGHA 18, 1947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


skill and qualifications when he attains the age of 18 years. During the period the male dependant is on live roster, the 
female dependant will be paid monetary compensation as per rates at paragraphs (i) & (i) above. This will be effective 
from 1.1.2000. 


Clause _ 9.5.0 (iv) of NCWA-VI provides that monetary compensation wherever applicable, would be paid till the 
female dependant attains the age of 60 years. 


In the instant case it is gathered from the pleadings of the union that no monetary compensation was paid to Kaloo 
Bhuia, the wife of the deceased employee and the union claimed monetary compensation for her till employment was 
granted to her son. Suggestion was given to the Workman Witness No. | that his mother did not submit any prayer for 
monetary compensation which the witness denied. In course of evidence union produced a copy of application dated 
11.05.2000 (Exhibit W-5) whereby Kaloo Bhuia requested the Manager of Kuardi Colliery to grant her Monthly 
Monetary Cash Compensation until employment was given to her son. Such evidence on record proves that the wife 
of the deceased was not paid monetary compensation though within a short period from the date of death of her 
husband she had applied before the management for payment of monetary compensation. Therefore, management is 
duty bound to comply the provisions of NCWA and pay monetary compensation to the wife of the deceased employee 
which is contingent to the relief of delayed employment to a male dependent. Since the question relating to non- 
payment of monetary compensation to the deceased has not been referred in the Schedule for adjudication by this 
Tribunal, I am not inclined to pass any specific order in favour of the wife of the deceased employee for payment of 
monetary compensation to her in view of the ratio of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court at Calcutta in the case of 
Axis Bank Vs. Union of India and Others [(2022)(175) FLR 2571] wherein it is held : 


“ The Labour Tribunal under the Industrial Disputes Act has a limited authority and jurisdiction to proceed 
only with the reference arose from the conciliation proceeding and cannot travel beyond the scope of 
reference.” 


12. On adverting to the question of denial of employment to Sanjay Bhuia, it is necessary to consider whether 
the claim for employment is legally tenable. It may be gathered from the admitted position in the written statement of 
the management that Sanjay Bhuia submitted application for his employment on 16.10.2000 which was found 
incomplete due to want of some documents. Accordingly, Sanjay Bhuia was advised to submit a complete application 
along with requisite documents. The dependent son further submitted application on 23.10.2000 and then again on 
12.07.2001. From Exhibit W-4, a letter dated 28.04.2000, I find that Kaloo Bhuia informed the Manager, Kuardi 
Colliery about the death of her husband and requested for providing employment to her son Sanjay Bhuia. Once again 
on 11.05.2000, the wife of the deceased submitted another application (Exhibit W-5), seeking monetary compensation 
for herself till employment was provided to her son. The application submitted by Sanjay Bhuia on 16.10.2000 
(Exhibit M-4) is indeed a continuation of the claim, already submitted by his mother. The management of ECL 
therefore could not have dismissed the application of the dependent son as time-barred. Management produced a letter 
dated 19.07.2001 (Exhibit M-7) wherein it is stated that Sanjay Bhuia applied for his employment after lapse of six 
months from the date of death of his father and as per guidelines of Director (Personnel), ECL, his claim for 
employment could not be considered. The management of ECL has not produced any copy of the Circular whereby 
the dependent of a deceased employee could be debarred from submitting application beyond a period of six months. 
If for argument’s sake any such circular has been issued by the Director (Personnel), ECL, the same cannot have any 
binding effect on the dependent of the deceased employee of ECL, as it is an outcome of a unilateral decision of the 
management and serves only as an untenable and arbitrary imposition upon employee. Such terms lying down the 
time-limit for submitting application for employment have not been provided in the NCWA. Therefore, any attempt to 
introduce any additional terms in relation to any subject matter already contained in NCWA cannot be legally binding 
unless such terms is ratified, accepted and adopted by the beneficiaries, who are the employees and their unions. 


13. In the case of Sukumoni Hembram alias Sukumoni Mejhan Vs. Union of India and Others [MAT 27 of 
2024] the Hon’ble Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court at Calcutta observed : 


“ None of the clauses 9.3.0 to 9.5.0 of NCWA provide any time limit for applying or prescribe any financial 
solvency of the family as a disqualification. It does not allow the employer to choose between the dependents as 
to who it would grant the employment or the MMCC.” 


In view of such observation and the contents of NCWA, I hold that the letter dated 19.07.2001, regretting the claim 
for employment of Sanjay Bhuia is contrary to the terms of agreement for providing employment and the same is not 
legally tenable. It transpires from the letter dated 19.07.2001 (Exhibit M-7) that Sanjay Bhuia submitted Indemnity 
Bond on 12.07.2001, after lapse of ten months for which there was a delay. From the letter of the Assistant Labour 
Commissioner (C), Raniganj at Durgapur dated 08.11.2023 it appears that much time was consumed by the 
management seeking Indemnity Bond and thereafter rejecting the same on the ground that one of the sureties who 
signed the Indemnity Bond was having less than five years of service and the Personnel Manager (Employment), ECL 
Headquarters informed the Assistant Personnel Manager, Satgram Area for directing the dependent for submitting a 
fresh Indemnity Bond and the dependent son submitted fresh Indemnity Bond with new surety, a permanent employee 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : फरवरी 7, 2026/माध 18, 1947 679 


having more than five years of service. Once again it appears to me that there is no specific rule for seeking any 
Indemnity Bond from the dependent of the deceased employee for the purpose of his employment. The management 
of the employer company is duty-bound to provide employment to the dependent son only on fulfilment of the 
essential criteria i.e., he should be a major, not more than thirty-five years and that he would be provided with 
employment commensurate to his skill and qualification. There is no procedural mandate for seeking Indemnity 
Bonds from the dependent requiring it to be signed by sureties who are the permanent employees of the company, 
having more than five years of service. The management of ECL appears to have delayed the entire process of 
providing employment by insisting upon compliance of tertiary requirement which cannot be any decisive factor for 
allowing or disallowing employment to the dependent. Therefore, delay caused by the management of ECL in seeking 
Indemnity Bond and further Indemnity Bond have prolonged the entire process and thereby lost sight of the actual 
purpose. This approach has caused severe hardship to the family of the dependent waiting for employment for several 
years. It appears from the record that the management of ECL held screening of the family members of the deceased 
employee on 22.02.2003 (Exhibit W-7) i.e., after issuing the first letter dated 19.07.2001, regretting the prayer for 
employment (Exhibit M-7). Management Witness No. 1 in his cross-examination has admitted that examination by 
the IME Board and screening of Sanjay Bhuia was held in the year 2003. Management did not disqualify Sanjay 
Bhuia on the ground of medical unfitness nor for being over-age. The only objection of the 


management is that the application for employment was submitted after passage of six months which is far from truth. 
Its need to be borne in mind that once the application has been submitted within a reasonable time, the management 
of employer company is duty-bound to process the same within reasonable time at their end. Fulfilling other 
requirements are to be treated as a continuing process relating back to the first application submitted by Kaloo Bhuia, 
the wife of the deceased and cannot be treated in isolation. Therefore, in my considered view the management’s 
decision to turn down the claim for employment of the dependent son on a plea that the application was made after six 
months is unjust and untenable. The management of ECL is a party to NCWA and it should be conscious of the fact 
that the terms which have been laid down have to be treated as enabling provisions and the same has to be strictly 
complied without any alteration / addition / novation on their part in the absence of the other party i.e., the union 
representing the employees. There is no scope for the employer company to deny employment to Sanjay Bhuia on the 
ground of delay in submitting his complete application if the other facts regarding his age and medical fitness have 
been satisfied. In such view of the matter, I hold that the action of the management in denying employment to Sanjay 
Bhuia is arbitrary, unjust and illegal. The management is directed to complete the employment procedure of Sanjay 
Bhuia within one month from the date of communication of the Award, in default, management shall pay 
compensation of an amount equivalent to the last salary drawn by Gokul Bhuia, each month till the dependent son is 
provided with employment. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against the management of Eastern Coalfields Limited. The 
denial of employment of Sanjay Bhuia on the ground of delay is not sustainable under the law and terms of National 
Coal Wage Agreement. The management of Eastern Coalfields Limited is directed to complete the procedural 
formalities to provide employment within one month from the date of communication of the Award, in default, 
management shall pay compensation of an amount equivalent to the last salary drawn by Gokul Bhuia, each month till 
he is provided with employment. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of the Award in 
duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for information and Notification.

PARTIES: Ganesh Turi 
(dependent son of Late Shanti Turi) 
Vs. 
Management of Jambad OCP, ECL 
REPRESENTATIVES: 
For the Union/Workman: Mr. Milan Kumar Bandyopadhyay, Advocate. 
For the Management of ECL: Mr. P. K. Das, Advocate. 
INDUSTRY: Coal. 
STATE: West Bengal.

AWARD 
In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (1) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 10 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-22012/185/2012-IR(CM-ID) dated 19.11.2012 has been pleased to refer the scheduled dispute between the 
employer, that is the Management of Jambad OCP under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited and their 
workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


“Whether the action of the management of Jambad OCP in denying employment to the dependent of Late 
Shanti Turi, Ex-Employee is justified? What relief the dependent concerned is entitled to and from 


682 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : FEBRUARY 7, 2026/MAGHA 18, 1947 [Part II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


which date ? ” 


1. On failure of conciliation before the Assistant Labour Commissioner (C), Raniganj at Durgapur, the 
Government of India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi referred the Industrial Dispute bearing Order 
No. L-22012/185/2012-IR(CM-II) dated 19.11.2012 to this Tribunal for adjudication. A Reference case was 
registered on 10.12.2012 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing 
them to appear and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. After service of Notice Ganesh Turi, claiming himself to be the youngest son of Shanti Turi, ex-employee 
filed statement of claim on behalf of the workman. United Koila Mazdoor Sangh (UTUC), the union which raised the 
Industrial Dispute did not take any step. The case of the workman as disclosed in the written statement dated 
04.06.2015 is that Shanti Turi, wife of Late Nibaran Turi was a permanent employee of Eastern Coalfields Limited 
(hereinafter referred to as ECL) and was posted at Jambad OCP under Kajora Area as Haulage Kamin bearing U.M. 
No. 537332. She was appointed in the service of the company on 15.01.1983 and died on 19.11.1994 while in service, 
leaving behind her two sons namely, Haglu Turi and Ganesh Turi. Haglu Turi is physically handicapped. The names 
of the sons appeared in the Service Record Excerpt of Shanti Turi as her dependents and she nominated her sons for 
receiving Coal Mines Provident Fund and Gratuity amount. After death of Shanti Turi, Ganesh Turi submitted an 
application along with relevant documents for his employment on compassionate ground against death of his mother 
as per provisions of National Coal Wage Agreement (hereinafter referred to as NCWA). The grievance of the 
dependent son is that the management did not consider his case for employment and such non-consideration amounts 
to denial of employment which is illegal and unjustified. Ganesh Turi in his written statement has prayed for passing 
an order in his favour, directing management of ECL to provide employment to him at the earliest. 


3. Management of ECL rebutted the claim of the dependent son of the deceased employee by filing a written 
statement on 08.11.2016. It is contended that the terms of reference is misconceived and the claim for employment is 
not in accordance with the provision of NCWA. Management further contended that Ganesh Turi did not submit 
relevant documents in support of his claim that he is the dependent son of the deceased employee or fulfilled all pre- 
requisites under the provisions of NCWA. In the written statement management claim that it is totally justified in not 
providing employment to the dependent of the deceased employee. 


4. The point for adjudication is whether the management of ECL is justified in denying employment to the 
dependent of Late Shanti Turi. 


>: The case was fixed up for evidence since 24.01.2017. Ganesh Turi filed his affidavit-in-chief but did not 
appear for his cross-examination. Several opportunities were granted to the workman for his evidence till 11.06.2024. 
Workman Witness did not turn up for his cross-examination and Mr. Ashish Mohan was examined as Management 
Witness No. 1. He filed his affidavit-in-chief and produced documents which have been marked as Exhibit M-1 to M- 
4. The witness was cross-examined on behalf of Ganesh Turi, claiming to be dependent son of Shanti Turi. 


6. In the affidavit-in-chief Ganesh Turi disclosed that his mother Shanti Turi was a permanent employee of 
ECL at Jambad OCP under Kajora Area of ECL. She died on 19.11.1994 while in the service of the company leaving 
behind him and Haglu Turi, his elder brother as the legal heirs and dependents. Their names are recorded in the 
Service Record Excerpt of their mother. It transpires from his statement that Haglu Turi was handicapped and for 
such reason Ganesh Turi applied for his employment before ECL on consent of his elder brother. The witness claimed 
to have submitted all relevant documents but management did not consider his prayer. The witness did not face the 
cross-examination. Therefore, apart from what is already admitted by the management in their written statements, 
other assertions made in the affidavit-in-chief by Ganesh Turi cannot be considered to have been proved. 


ils Mr. Ashish Mohan, Deputy Manager (Personnel), Jambad OCP has been examined as Management Witness 
No. 1. He filed his affidavit-in-chief relating to the management’s case wherein he admitted that Shanti Turi was an 
employee of ECL who died on 19.11.1994 while in service of the company. It appears from his statement that at first 
Haglu Turi submitted application for employment on 20.03.1997 but as he is physically handicapped such claim was 
not considered by the management. Late Ganesh Turi submitted a separate application on 01.07.2010 for his 
employment i.e., after a long delay. Management witness further stated that as Ganesh Turi was a minor, his claims 
could not be considered by the management and there is no scope to keep his name in the Live Roster of the company 
as per provisions of NCWA. In course of his evidence management witness produced the following documents : 


(i) Copy of the application of Haglu Turi dated 20.03.1997 addressed to the Agent, Jambad OCP, 
claiming employment against the death of his mother is produced as Exhibit M-1. 


(ii) Copy of the Service Record Excerpt of Shanti Turi, as Exhibit M-2. 
(ili) Copy of the Death Registration Certificate of Shanti Turi, as Exhibit M-3 


(iv) Copy of the application of Ganesh Turi addressed to the Agent, Jambad OCP, claiming 
employment, as Exhibit M-4. 


8. In course of cross-examination the management witness admitted that there is a provision for providing 
employment to the physically handicapped person in ECL. He further stated that earlier when the son of Shanti Turi 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : फरवरी 7, 2026/माध 18, 1947 683 


applied for employment, management did not consider the percentage of his disability as he is physically 
handicapped. Apart from application of Ganesh Turi management had no other document to show that any decision 
was taken by the management regarding his prayer for employment. 


9. The case was fixed up on 21.11.2025 for argument but in view of Ministry’s letter No. Z-25025/01/2025- 
CLS-I(E) dated 14.05.2025 to take up old cases for disposal during the special campaign, Notice was issued under 
registered post to both parties, fixing the case for haring of argument. Notice was sent to the General Secretary of 
United Koila Mazdoor Sangh (UTUC) but the same was returned unserved. No Notice was sent to Ganesh Turi at his 
address available in his affidavit-in-chief. 


10. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management of ECL submitted that Haglu Turi who claimed 
employment after the death of his mother by submitting his application dated 20.03.1997 was physically handicapped 
and no employment was provided to him. Thereafter, the younger son Ganesh Turi submitted an application for his 
employment before the Agent of Jambad OCP on 01.07.2010 i.e., sixteen years after the death of his mother. Learned 
advocate argued that at the time of death of Shanti Turi on 19.11.1994 NCWA-V was applicable to the employees and 
management of ECL. To maintain the name of a minor dependent son in the Live Roster his age should have been 
fifteen years or more on the date of death of the employee. In the instant case the prayer for employment of Ganesh 
Turi could not be considered as his age was only eleven years at the time of death of his mother and his name could 
not have been maintained in the Live Roster. The application for employment made in the year 2010 therefore, could 
not be considered and the Industrial Dispute raised against the management is liable to be dismissed. 


11. On the date fixed for hearing of argument none appeared for Ganesh Turi after Notice. I have considered the 
materials on record, pleadings of the parties and the argument advanced on behalf of the management. Undisputedly, 
Haglu Turi and Ganesh Turi are the two dependent sons of Late Shanti Turi and their names appeared in the Service 
Record Excerpt, which is produced as Exhibit M-2. In the year 1987 the age of Ganesh Turi was four (4) years and 
Haglu Turi was thirteen (13) years. Initially, Haglu Turi submitted an application dated 20.03.1997 (Exhibit M-1) 
praying for his employment as a dependent. As he is handicapped, his brother submitted a separate application on 
01.07.2010 (Exhibit M-4), claiming employment for himself. In his application Ganesh Turi disclosed that he had 
submitted an application in the year 2003 for employment but the case file is still pending for consideration. Ganesh 
Turi did not state the exact date of his application made in the year 2003. No such document has come forth for 
consideration. It is noteworthy that by submitting a second claim by Ganesh Turi on 01.07.2010, the claim for 
employment of Haglu Turi was waived. According to Clause 9.5.0 (iii) of NCWA-V which was in force from 
01.07.1991 to 30.06.1996, in case of death of an employee either in mine accident or for other reasons or medical 
unfitness under Clause 9.4.0, if no employment has been offered and the male dependant of the concerned worker is 
fifteen (15) years and above in age he would be kept on a live roster and would be provided with employment 
commensurate with his skill and qualifications when he attains the age of 18 years. During the period the male 
dependant is on live roster, the female dependant will be paid monetary compensation as per rates in Paragraphs (i) & 
(ii). It is crystal clear from the provisions of NCWA that Ganesh Turi was not eligible for employment even on his 
attaining majority as he was only eleven (11) years of age at the time of death of his mother and fell short of four (4) 
years to fulfill the required condition for being considered for employment on being attaining majority. 


12. The provisions of NCWA are strictly followed for the purpose of considering eligibility of a dependent for 
employment. There cannot be any deviation from such rules. In the case of Sukumoni Hembram alias Sukumoni 
Mejhan Vs. Union of India and Others [MAT 27 of 2024] the Hon’ble Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court 
at Calcutta held : 


“ NCWA is a negotiated agreement that has been arrived at between the employer and the employees. It is a 
settlement under section 2 (p) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 and has binding effect on the parties thereto 
under section 18 (3) of the Act of 1947.” 


13. Under the fact and circumstances, I hold that Ganesh Turi, the dependent son is not entitled to any 
employment under the management of ECL on account of death of his mother in harness. The issue relating to 
employment of Haglu Turi does not arise in this case as neither the union nor Haglu Turi himself appeared before the 
Tribunal to assert his claim. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is dismissed on contest. Ganesh Turi, the dependent son of Late Shanti Turi is not 
entitled to get employment under Eastern Coalfields Limited as per provisions of National Coal Wage Agreement — 
V. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the 
Ministry of Labour, Government of India, New Delhi for information and Notification.

AWARD 
In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (1) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 10 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-22012/459/1998-IR(C-II) dated 28.04.2004 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer, that is the Management of Dhemomain Colliery under Sodepur Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited and 
their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


“Whether the action of the management of Dhemomain Colliery of M/s. ECL in denying employment to Shri 
Ramashray, son-in-law of Shri Bairagi Harijan, ex-employee is legal and justified? If not, to what relief the 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : फरवरी 7, 2026/माध 18, 1947 685 


workman ts entitled? ” 


1. On receiving Order No. L-22012/459/1998-IR(C-II) dated 28.04.2004 from the Government of India, 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 19.05.2004 and an 
order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear and submit their 
written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. The union of Koyala Mazdoor Congress filed written statement on 20.08.2004. Fact of the cases which 
unfolds from the written statement is that Bairagi Harijan was posted as Timber Mazdoor at Dhemomain Colliery 
under Eastern Coalfields Limited (hereinafter referred to as ECL). He was suffering from illness and the Area 
Medical Board declared him medically unfit for duty on 17.07.1992. The employer company terminated Bairagi 
Harijan from service w.e.f. 23.07.1992 as per provisions of Clause 9.4.0 of National Coal Wage Agreement — IV one 
dependent of the employee who lost his service on account of disablement is entitled to employment under the 
company provided the employee is within fifty-eight (58) years of age and he should have two years of service left. 
At the relevant time Bairagi Harijan had Ramashray Ram his dependent son-in-law and nominated him for 
employment. He also submitted his application and relevant documents for employment of his son-in-law. 
Management held screening of documents and forwarded the proposal for employment to ECL Headquarters through 
Area Office. The management verified the relationship between Ramashray Ram and Bairagi Harijan through Police 
from his native place and the same was confirmed. It is contended that in violation of provisions of National Coal 
Wage Agreement (hereinafter referred to as NCWA) management did not provide any employment to the dependent 
son-in-law. According to the union the act of the management is unjust and necessary direction should be given to the 
employer company to provide employment to Ramashray Ram without further delay. 


3. After several opportunities management failed to file any written statement until 08.05.2023, for nineteen 
years. The specific case of the management as per their written statement is that Bairagi Harijan, an employee of ECL 
at Dhemomain Colliery was declared medically unfit by the Area Medical Board and his service was terminated by 
the management on 23.07.1992. The ex-employee nominated his son-in-law to provide employment in his place as 
per provisions of NCWA. As the relationship of alleged son-in-law and the ex-workman was not sufficiently 
established, the claim for employment was not considered by the management. According to the management the 
relationship between the alleged son-in-law and the workman was doubtful. Therefore, management was unable to 
provide employment. It is claimed that the decision of the management is proper and the nominated person is not 
entitled to any relief. 


4. The only question for consideration is whether management of Dhemomain Colliery is justified in denying 
employment to Ramashray Ram, claiming to be son-in-law of Bairagi Harijan. 


5. During pendency of the case Bairagi Harijan died on 14.11.2014. In the instant case Ramashray Ram has 
been examined as Workman Witness No. |. He filed an affidavit-in-chief where from it appears that in September 
2023, he was 49 years of age. The witness stated that he is the son-in-law of Bairagi Harijan. His father-in-law was 
examined by Medical Board constituted by the company and was declared medically unfit on 17.07.1992. The 
company terminated the service of Bairagi Harijan on 23.07.1992. The witness further deposed that his father-in-law 
submitted an application claiming employment for him as son-in-law and also submitted relevant documents. The 
employment proposal was processed and after proper screening at Colliery and Area Level it was forwarded to the 
ECL Headquarters. The management verified the relationship between Bairagi Harijan and Ramashray Ram, seeking 
verification through Police authority, who confirmed that Ramashray Ram is the son-in-law of Bairagi Harijan. The 
management thereafter did not provide employment to the dependent son-in-law. It is stated that he has no means of 
livelihood and requires employment. The witness further stated that he was wholly dependent on the earing of Bairagi 
Harijan, who died on 14.11.2014, leaving behind his daughter Smt. Bechni Debi and Ramashray Ram, the son-in-law. 
Witness further stated that he was residing in the house of his father-in-law during his lifetime and now at his native 
village with other family members. It is stated that Bairagi Harijan had no son and Bechni Devi is the only daughter 
who has been married to him during the lifetime of his father-in-law. In course of his examination-in-chief the 
workman witness produced the following documents in support of his case : 


(i) Photocopy of Order dated 20/23.07.1992 whereby Bairagi Harijan was declared medically unfit is 
produced as Exhibit W-1. 


(ii) Photocopy of the application submitted by Bairagi Harijan on 25.03.1993 for employment of 
Ramashray Ram, as Exhibit W-2. 


(iii) Photocopy of the letter dated 01.12.1993 which was issued by the Dy. CME/Agent, Dhemomain 
Colliery to Ramashray Ram for appearing before the Screening Committee, as Exhibit W-3. 


(iv) Photocopy of another letter whereby Ramashray Ram was asked to appear before the Screening 
Committee once again on 22.01.1994, as Exhibit W-4. 


(v) Photocopy of the Marriage Certificate of Ramashray Ram issued by the Marriage Officer, Asansol, 
as Exhibit W-5. 


(vi) Photocopy of Police Report dated 06.11.1995 issued by the Superintendent of Police, Azamgarh, as 


686 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : FEBRUARY 7, 2026/MAGHA 18, 1947 [Part II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


Exhibit W-6. 


(vii) Photocopy of the Office Order dated 22.08.1996 whereby Ramashray Ram was asked to appear 
before the screening committee at Area Office on 24.08.1996, as Exhibit W-7. 


(Vili) Photocopy of the Letter dated 08/11.09.1995 whereby the union representative was informed that 
the prayer of Ramashray Ram would be considered after receiving Police Verification Report, as 
Exhibit W-8. 


6. In cross-examination the witness deposed that he got married to Bechni Debi on 23.05.1992 at Ramgarh 
(Azamgarh). It transpires from his cross-examination that his marriage was registered for the second time in the year 
1996 and a copy of Marriage Certificate was produced as Exhibit W-9 as he was asked to produce Marriage 
Certificate for the second time. In cross-examination Ramashray Ram stated that he was married before his father-in- 
law was declared medically unfit. He further deposed that he continued to reside with his father-in-law at Dhemomain 
Colliery but he is not a Voter of Dhemomain. Witness denied the suggestion that he is not the son-in-law of Bairagi 
Harijan or he is not the dependent of Bairagi Harijan. 


7. Management produced no evidence in this case. 


8. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, President, Koyala Mazdoor Congress argued that management admitted the fact that 
Bairagi Harijan was an employee of ECL until he was declared medically unfit and terminated from his service. It is 
also established from the evidence on record that an application was submitted by the ex-employee on 25.03.1993 for 
employment of Ramashray Ram, his son-in-law which has been marked as Exhibit W-2. The management on the 
basis of such application asked Ramashray Ram to appear before the Screening Committee on 04.12.1993 by issuing 
letter dated 01.12.1993 (Exhibit W-3). He was again directed to appear before the Screening Committee on 
22.01.1994 (Exhibit W-4) and for the third time on 24.08.1996 by letter dated 22.08.1996 (Exhibit W-7). Mr. Kumar 
submitted that the management verified the relationship between the ex-employee and Ramashray Ram and the 
Superintendent of Police, Azamgarh, Uttar Pradesh by letter dated 06.11.1995 addressed to the Agent, Dhemomain 
Colliery (Exhibit W-6) informed that Ramashray Ram is the son-in-law of Bairagi Harijan, but management neither 
allowed the proposal for employment nor regret the claim. Mr. Kumar submitted that according to the provisions of 
NCWA the dependent son-in-law who has been nominated by the employee should be provided with employment. 


9. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management of ECL argued that Ramashray Ram in his affidavit-in- 
chief has stated that he married Bechni Debi, the daughter of Bairagi Harijan on 23.05.1992 but in the Certificate of 
Marriage (Exhibit W-5) it is stated that the marriage took place on 187 day of March, 1993. Learned advocate for the 
management argued that this Marriage Certificate has been prepared only for making a claim for employment after 
the ex-employee was terminated from his service on 23.07.1992. It is further argued that the union has failed to 
prove that Ramashray Ram is the dependent son-in-law of the ex-employee, Bairagi Harijan. Referring to 
Exhibit W-6, Mr. Das submitted that the Police at Azamgarh after holding enquiry submitted a report to the Agent of 
Dhemomain Colliery dated 06.11.1995 only informing that there was no adverse report against Ramashray Ram, son 
of Sabhuti Ram, Vill- Rampur Katharawa, PO- Devgaon, Dist- Azamgarh and the report does not establish the 
relationship between Bairagi Harijan and Ramashray Ram as father-in-law and son-in-law. It is strenuously argued 
that the alleged son-in-law could not establish his relationship with the ex-employee. The management is not in a 
position to provide employment to Ramashray Ram and urged that the Industrial Dispute is liable to be dismissed. 


10. I have carefully considered the pleadings of the parties, evidence adduced by the workman witness, 
documents produced and the argument advanced on behalf of the management and union in support of their 
respective cases. The material on record and the admitted position of this case makes it abundantly clear that Bairagi 
Harijan, the ex-employee of ECL was posted at Dhemomain Colliery and terminated from his service on 23.07.1992 
on the ground of his being declared medically unfit. It is also admitted that as per the provisions of Clause 9.4.0 of 
NCWA-V a dependent of the employee who is declared medically unfit, is entitled to employment under the 
employer company provided that the concerned employee was below fifty-eight years of age. In the instant case no 
dispute has been raised by the management that the ex-employee was above the age of fifty-eight (58) years or that 
the dependent of such employee is not entitled to any employment. In the present case the concerned workman 
submitted an application on 25.03.1993 addressed to the Welfare Officer of Dnemomain Colliery for employment of 
one Ramashray Ram, describing him as his son-in-law (Exhibit W-2). Clause 9.4.0 (iii) of NCWA-V provides that for 
the purpose of being considered as dependent, wife / husband as the case may be, unmarried daughter, son and legally 
adopted son may be considered for employment but if no such direct dependant is available for employment younger 
brother, widowed daughter / widowed daughter-in-law or son-in-law residing with the employee and almost wholly 
dependent on the earning of the employees may be considered for employment. From the evidence on record, it 
appears that Ramashray Ram was directed to appear before the Screening Committee on three occasions by issuing 
letters which have been marked as Exhibit W-3, W-4 and W-7. Management called for Police report from Azamgarh, 
Uttar Pradesh to find out if there was any relationship between Bairagi Harijan and Ramashray Ram. A letter dated 
06.11.1995 was issued by the Superintendent of Police, Azamgarh which is absolutely silent about the relationship 
between Ramashray Ram and Bairagi Harijan. It is only mentioned that there was no adverse report regarding 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : फरवरी 7, 2026/माध 18, 1947 687 


character and antecedents of Ramashray Ram. At the time of hearing this case Bairagi Harijan had expired. 
Ramashray Ram did not examine Bechni Debi, the daughter of Late Bairagi Harijan to support his case. In his cross - 
examination the workman witness deposed that he got married to Bechni Debi, the daughter of Bairagi Harijan on 
23.05.1992 and he produced the Marriage Certificate dated 16.01.1996/20.02.1996 only because he was asked to 
submit Marriage Certificate. On a perusal of Marriage Certificate (Exhibit W-5), I find that the marriage under the 
Special Marriage Act, 1954 took place and was registered on 18.03.1993, which was much after the termination of 
service of Bairagi Harijan on 23.07.1992. If the subsequent marriage registration under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 
dated 20.02.1996 is considered, it would appear that the alleged Hindu Marriage took place on 23.05.1992 (Exhibit 
W-9), that is only two months before the date of termination. The date of marriage in the two documents apparently 
contradict each other, raising doubt. The daughter of Bairagi Harijan was not examined as a witness to set this issue at 
rest and establish their relationship. Therefore, it can safely be held that there was no marriage prior to declaring 
Bairagi Harijan medically unfit. There is no evidence on record to establish that a relationship of son-in-law and 
father-in-law subsisted between Ramashray Ram and Bairagi Harijan. Accordingly, the management of ECL has 
committed no illegality in not processing the claim for employment of Ramashray Ram as a dependent of Bairagi 
Harijan. I find no merit in the case and the same is dismissed on contest. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is dismissed on contest against the union. The action of the management of 
Dhemomain Colliery under Sodepur Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited in not providing employment to Ramashray 
Ram as dependent son-in-law of Bairagi Harijan calls for no interference. Let an award be drawn up in light of my 
above findings. Let copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour, Government of India, New 
Delhi for information and Notification.

AWARD 


In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (1) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 10 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order 
No. L-22012/104/2022-IR(CM-IID) dated 19/12/2022 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the 
employer, that is the Management of Mouthdih Unit, Sodepur (R) Colliery, Sodepur Area of Eastern Coalfields 
Limited and their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


“Whether the action of the Management of M/s. Eastern Coalfields Ltd. in relation to its Mouthdih Unit, 
Sodepur (R) Colliery under Sodepur Area in dismissing the service of Shri Manoj Kumar Nunia, UG Loader, 
U.M. No. 102596 vide their letter No. PD/C-6/17/36/155/001876 dated 05-14/10/2017 is fair, legal and 
Justified? If not, to what relief the concerned workman is entitled to?” 


1. On receiving Order No. L-22012/104/2022-IR(CM-II) dated 19/12/2022 from the Government of India, 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case No. 02 of 2023 was registered on 
05/01/2023 and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to appear 
and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2. General Secretary, Koyala Mazdoor Congress filed written statement for Manoj Kumar Nunia, ex-employee 
of ECL on 02/05/2023. In nutshell, facts of the case as disclosed in the written statement is that Manoj Kumar Nunia 
was a permanent employee of ECL and was posted as an Underground Loader at Mouthdih Unit, Sodepur (R) 
Colliery, ECL. Workman was absent from duty due to his serious illness which was beyond his control and he was 
unable to perform the duty from 28/11/2015 to 20/04/2016 i.e. a period for less than five months. During his absence 
from duty, he underwent medical treatment. When Manoj Kumar Nunia reported for duty, management of the colliery 
issued charge sheet against him bearing No. SC/C-6/F-07/2016/0870 dated 21/25.04.2016. Management thereafter 
held departmental enquiry against the workman and finally issued an order of dismissal bearing No. PD/C- 
6/17/36/155/001876 dated 05/14.10.2017, dismissing the workman from service. Dismissed workman thereafter 
submitted mercy appeal and prayed for allowing him to join duty. According to the union, absence of Manoj Kumar 
Nunia from duty was beyond his control and he was not given ample opportunity to defend himself. Enquiry Officer 
did not consider medical certificates submitted by the workman during enquiry proceeding. Furthermore, charged 
employee was not allowed to avail assistance of co-workers during enquiry. Signature of the workman was obtained 
on documents and on conclusion of enquiry, workman was found guilty of misconduct. Taking advantage of illiteracy 
of the workman and without considering the treatment papers, Enquiry Officer held the enquiry in violation of the 
principle of Natural Justice. It is prayed that workman may be reinstated in service and back wages paid to him for the 
period of his unintentional absence from duty and the period of his termination. 


3 Management of ECL contested the reference by filing written statement on 21/03/2023 where it is disclosed 
that Manoj Kumar Nunia was absent from duty from 28/11/2015 to 20/04/2016 for which charge sheet was issued 
against him on 21/04/2016 under clauses 26.29, 26.23, 26.05 and 26.22 i.e. for unauthorized absence from duty 
beyond ten days, habitual absence from duty without sufficient cause, willful neglect of work and sabotage or causing 
willful damage to work in progress or to property of the company respectively. Mr. Ravi Bara, Asst. Manager (Per) 
was appointed as the Enquiry Officer for holding enquiry in respect of the charges levelled against Manoj Kumar 
Nunia. Enquiry Officer provided opportunity to the workman to defend his case, holding enquiry on 05/05/2017, 
09/05/2017 and 16/05/2017. Workman participated in the enquiry and defended himself. Enquiry Officer observed the 
principle of Natural Justice during holding the enquiry. From office record, it would appear that on previous three 
years, attendance of the workman was poor. In the year 2013, the workman attended duty for only twelve days, in the 
year 2014 his attendance was NIL and in the year 2016 until issuance of charge sheet he attended duty for six days 
only. After completion of the enquiry proceeding, report was submitted to the Disciplinary Authority. The 
Disciplinary Authority issued a second show cause Notice bearing No. PD/C-6/17/Absenteeism/3/788 dated 
09/06/2017 which was sent to the concerned workman through registered post. Workman did not reply to the second 
show cause Notice and he was finally dismissed from service by the Disciplinary Authority. Management contended 
that the quantum of punishment passed against the workman is proportionate to the nature of misconduct and he is not 
entitled to any relief.
